entities.summary: Pope Honorius II, born Lamberto Scannabecchi, was head of the Catholic Church and ruler of the Papal States from 21 December 1124 to his death in 1130. He played a crucial role in the Investiture Controversy, a defining conflict between the Catholic Church and the Holy Roman Empire. During his papacy, Honorius II implemented various reforms, including the establishment of the Congregation of Cardinals, which aimed to increase the papacy's power and authority. He also engaged in diplomatic efforts to secure the support of the Norman Kingdom in southern Italy. Honorius II's papacy was marked by the rise of the Hohenstaufen dynasty, which would eventually produce emperors such as Frederick I and Frederick II. The Pope's legacy includes the creation of the Curia Romana, the central administrative body of the Catholic Church, and the shaping of the medieval Papal States' politics and economy. The impact of Honorius II's reign can be seen in the subsequent power struggles between the Catholic Church and the Holy Roman Empire, as well as the emergence of the Franciscan and Dominican orders, which would play significant roles in the development of Western Christianity.
